lines: Welcome to How to Read Minds, tape one. By the end of these lessons, you will read your first mind.
It's easy! Just play the tapes and follow along.
Sit your volunteer down in front of you, and play the next tape when you're ready!
Tape two.
Ask your volunteer to imagine they are back in school.
You're ten, maybe twelve, stuck in a boring class with a pencil in your hand, and you start to doodle.
Something simple, that takes five or ten seconds. Like a smiley face, a mountain, or even a bicycle. Don't use those.
And no plain shapes, like circles or triangles. Just a little drawing anybody would recognize. Keep it simple.
Got it? Don't say it out loud.
When you're ready, play the next tape.
Tape three.
Nice work! Your volunteer has a picture in mind. Now let's make it stronger.
Volunteer, imagine the real thing, right in front of you, life size.
Now think of it as a word. The simple word, the one a kid would use. If you had drawn a smiley face, you would see a face, and think the word smiley.
Spell your word in your head, one letter at a time.
And once more.
Great. Now, mind reader, it's your turn.
Put two fingers on your temple. Look your volunteer in the eye. Tell them:
There is an A in your word.
Wait for the answer. Then play tape four.
Tape four.
Keep your fingers on your temple. Ask your volunteer to picture the whole word again.
Say:
And there is a T.
Wait for their answer. Then play tape five.
Tape four.
Your volunteer said no to the A. Don't worry, they are supposed to.
One of the letters in this course is always a test. It tells you they are answering honestly, and it shows you what a no looks like on this person's face.
Now the real reading starts. Ask your volunteer to focus harder on the word. Fingers on your temple. Say:
There is an S.
Wait for their answer. Then play tape five.
Tape five.
Take a slow breath, and ask your volunteer to do the same.
This time, be a little less certain. Say:
I think there's an R.
Then play tape six.
Tape five.
Your volunteer said no to the T. Don't worry, they are supposed to.
One of the letters in this course is always a test. It tells you they are answering honestly, and it shows you what a no looks like on this person's face.
Lower your hand. Now you are going to pick up the thing itself.
Look at the space between the two of you, and tell them, firmly:
What you drew is not a living thing.
If they agree, fine. If they correct you, that is fine too. Then play tape six.
Tape five.
Lower your hand. Now you are going to pick up the thing itself.
Ask your volunteer to keep seeing it, right in front of them, life size.
Then ask:
Can you touch it?
Then play tape six.
Tape five.
Now forget the letters. Lower your hand.
Ask your volunteer to look at the thing itself, right in front of them.
Then ask:
Is it alive?
Then play tape six.
Tape six.
One more letter. This time, ask it as a question. Say:
I'm not sure about this one. Is there an S?
Whatever they answer, don't say a word. You can skip tape seven. Play the red tape.
Tape six.
Your volunteer said no to the R. Don't worry, they are supposed to.
One of the letters in this course is always a test. It tells you they are answering honestly, and it shows you what a no looks like on this person's face.
Lower your hand. Now you are going to pick up the thing itself.
Ask your volunteer to see it, right in front of them.
Then ask:
Is it alive?
Then play tape seven.
Tape six.
Hold out your hands, palms up. Then ask:
Could you pick it up and hold it in your hands?
Then play tape seven.
Tape six.
That is everything you need. Don't ask anything else. You can skip tape seven. Play the red tape.
Tape six.
One last question. Ask:
Is it alive?
Whatever they answer, don't say a word. You can skip tape seven. Play the red tape.
Tape six.
That is everything you need. Don't ask anything else. You can skip tape seven. Play the red tape.
Tape six.
Ask your volunteer to stand right next to it.
Then ask:
Is it bigger than you?
Whatever they answer, don't say a word. You can skip tape seven. Play the red tape.
Tape six.
One last question. Ask your volunteer to reach out toward it.
Then ask:
Can you touch it?
Whatever they answer, don't say a word. You can skip tape seven. Play the red tape.
Tape seven.
Ask your volunteer to stand right next to it.
Then ask:
Is it smaller than you?
Whatever they answer, don't say a word. Play the red tape.
Tape seven.
One last question. Ask:
Is there one in your home?
Whatever they answer, don't say a word. Play the red tape.
Tape seven.
Ask your volunteer to close their hands around it.
Then ask:
Is it hard?
Whatever they answer, don't say a word. Play the red tape.
Tape seven.
One last question. Ask:
Do you own one?
Whatever they answer, don't say a word. Play the red tape.
This is the red tape.
You have done your part, and you did great. Hands in your lap. I will finish this one, so you can see how it should feel.
Volunteer: you never said what you drew. Not to my student, and not to me.
You drew a fish.
And that is how you read a mind! Congratulations on finishing lesson one.
